body:
On Fri, 19 May 2000 19:48:55 +0100, "the endgame"
<end_game@chinning.com> wrote:

>Malcolm McMahon <malcolm@pigsty.demon.co.uk> wrote in message
>news:s1t8isgidpt87h8rfek00pi4chpfdv22qh@4ax.com...
>> On Thu, 18 May 2000 19:03:30 +0100, Nameless Wildness
>> <namelesswildness@subdimension.com> wrote:
>>
>> > At that stage the machines will be in effective control.
>> >People won't be able to just turn the machines off, because they will be
>> >so dependent on them that turning them off would amount to suicide.
>>
>> Substitute the word "society" for "the machines" and you'll see we are
>> already in that position.
>
>
>Society is an anachronism of feudal european monarchy. With the beginning of
>the industrial revolution the nepotistic dynastic hierarchy had to accept
>'unlanded' members in order to prevent instability within the 'system' (as
>it were).
>

The benfit of which, to most of us, is that every few years we
theoretically (if we happen to live in a marginal constituency) get to
influence a choice between two indistinguishable groups of politicians
who actually have remarkably little influence on events. Meanwhile a
complex web in ecconomic interaction, complex beyond the comprehension
of any single human being, actually determines the environment in which
we live.

And we are indeed so dependant on this complex web of ecconomic
interactions that to turn it off would ammount to suicide.

The difference between the industrial and the agricultural era is that
this web has become far more complex, so that it utilises the inteligent
decision making capacity of a far larger percentage of the population.
Humans, considered as part of the body of society, have been promoted
from muscle cells to neurons.

>The 'system' in the u.k. is now a purely capitalist function. "Society", I
>believe is torn between becoming part of the 'system' and sticking to the
>old 'class' values.
>

Quite true, but this spreading of the decision making function merely
dilutes the power of individual humans over historical events. In a
genuine monarchy we were, to some degree ruled by a human being. Now
we're ruled by a construct which _uses_ human beings without actually
obeying any of them.
